newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF member urges swift easing in rates -paper.
newsitem.headline: BoF member urges swift easing in rates -paper.

text.p: Paul Marchelli, a member of the Bank of France monetary policy council, was quoted in a French newspaper on Tuesday as calling for interest rates to be lowered as soon as possible.
In the interview with Liberation, Marchelli also criticised Germany's attachment to a "strong mark", saying it was dictated "largely by sentimental reasons".

Marchelli told Liberation "we should do everything possible to lower our interest rates as quickly as possible which would allow an acceleration of growth and (the franc) to find a suitable level against the dollar."
In the interview, Marchelli said he believed most European currencies were overvalued against the dollar and that the franc was overvalued "by about 10 percent".
He said that if France cuts its rates quickly to below German rates, "the markets will understand our strategy very well because the franc is in good shape."
The French intervention rate is currently at 3.20 percent while the German repo rate which it is considered to track is at 3.00 percent.
Marchelli's views, the newspaper noted, are opposed to those of Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet who believes such a move would lead to financial market turbulence.
